office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering the tax structure, natural-resource and timber policy, K-12 policy and funding, and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: An open seat, vacated by retiring Rep. Steve Tharinger, between independent Marcia Kelbon, a Quilcene fire commissioner and former biotech executive who led the primary, and Democrat Kaylee Kuehn, a Sequim former teacher and legislative aide. Kelbon stresses spending restraint, deregulation and opposition to the income tax; Kuehn stresses a less regressive tax code, climate investments and LGBTQ+ rights, and questions how an independent would be effective.

candidates.summary: Quilcene fire commissioner, engineer and patent attorney who spent 19 years as a biotech general counsel and executive; ran for state Senate as a Republican in 2024 and now runs as an independent.
highlights: Opposes the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and calls the state's finances a spending problem [S5]
Would revise the Growth Management Act and roll back energy-code costs to spur starter homes [S2][S7]
Would restore felony drug possession to push people into treatment [S5][S7]
Opposes transgender girls on girls' sports teams while backing marriage equality [S4]
Says she could caucus with either party and no party will drive her vote [S5]

taxes.basis: Opposes the 2026 income tax and pledges the state will not tax income, but said she could see a voter-approved graduated income tax paired with sales and property tax cuts.

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls it a spending problem, wants the budget reined in and essentials funded first with accountability requirements.

housing.basis: Statement, website and two forums call for trimming housing regulations, revising the Growth Management Act and rolling back the energy code.

safety.basis: At two forums called for restoring felony drug possession to steer people into treatment, and wants law enforcement empowered.

climate.basis: Said she would repeal the Climate Commitment Act (July) and later that it should at least be modified; calls warming serious and favors incentives over penalties.

experience.basis: No legislative service; local fire commissioner running as an independent outside the party caucuses, with long private-sector experience.

local-control.basis: Would reduce unfunded state mandates on counties.

reform.basis: Runs as an independent, says neither a party nor special interests will drive her vote and she would caucus case by case.

healthcare.basis: Said that nationally she supports getting insurance companies 'out of the mix completely'; also seeks critical-access status for Olympic Medical Center.

social.basis: Opposes transgender girls on girls' sports teams and supports women's 'safe spaces,' while backing marriage equality and anti-discrimination on sexuality.

candidates.summary: Sequim native, former high school teacher and state Senate legislative aide, and pulp and paper workers' advocate, making her first run for office as a Democrat.
highlights: Calls Washington's tax system regressive and wants a fairer one with spending accountability [S2][S8]
Supports emission-reduction policy and keeping Climate Commitment Act revenue for climate and rural projects [S2][S3]
Supports trans individuals and '100% bodily autonomy' [S2][S3]
Endorsed by the State Labor Council, the WEA and the district's Democratic legislators [S1][S2]

taxes.basis: Wants a fairer tax system that shifts burden from working people and fixed incomes; names no specific new tax.

spending.basis: Pairs spending accountability and 'throwing more money at education is not the answer' with calls to fully fund schools, special education and Medicaid rates.

housing.basis: Backs Housing Trust Fund investment and also pledges to streamline permitting and cut bureaucracy.

safety.basis: Treats addiction as a health issue while wanting to revisit a sentencing grid she says limits accountability, and backs law enforcement.

climate.basis: Supports emission-reduction policies and protecting Climate Commitment Act investments, with attention to leakage and in-state industrial jobs.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with legislative-staff experience, endorsed by the retiring incumbent and sitting district legislators.

immigration.basis: Platform opposes unconstitutional ICE actions and calls for due process; no further immigration proposals.

healthcare.basis: Proposals work within the current system (higher Medicaid and Medicare reimbursement, rural recruitment), though she has praised other countries' systems.

social.basis: Platform defends '100% bodily autonomy' and marriage rights; at a forum supported trans individuals and nonbinary athletes.
